macro.note: Dallas Fed-confirmed at 9:30 CT. July general business activity was +1.3 and production 10.1. There are no major US economic reports Monday, and one correction matters more than anything on the list: the Chicago Business Barometer is NOT due Monday. Some aggregators carry an Aug 31 row with a 57.8 figure; the issuer calendar puts it Friday Aug 28 at 9:45 ET, where it printed 47.1, DOWN 10.5 points from 57.6. What actually matters about Monday is that it is the August close, so month-end rebalancing and settlement flows run through the tape and the price action carries less information than usual. Aug 31 is a UK bank holiday, which thins London liquidity, but US markets hold a normal full session. 13-week and 26-week bill auctions

macro.event: ISM Manufacturing PMI and JOLTS job openings
macro.note: Both ISM-confirmed and BLS-confirmed for Sept 1 at 10:00 ET, and this is now the most interesting setup of the week. ISM manufacturing consensus is 55.1 against a July print of 55.6 - and that consensus has NOT repriced for Friday's Chicago collapse to 47.1. Regional surveys are noisy and Chicago is the noisiest of them, so this is an asymmetry rather than a forecast: if the national number follows Chicago down, it lands ten days before an FOMC the market has priced 59% for a HIKE. JOLTS resolved this run - the BLS September schedule states Tuesday Sept 1, 10:00 AM verbatim, so yesterday's Sep 2 conflict is closed and the Sep 2 listings are wrong. Consensus 7.4mn against 7.4mn prior. Construction spending the same morning, consensus -0.1%. Governor Barr speaks at 9:05 AM ET, also resolved this run on the Fed's own calendar; the 1:05 PM listings circulating on aggregators appear to be a timezone conversion error. Dell after the close

macro.event: Fed Beige Book; ADP employment 8:15 AM and factory orders
macro.note: Fed and ADP both issuer-confirmed. July ADP was plus 44,000 with June revised to plus 95,000; consensus is plus 45,000 from three economists. Factory orders consensus is plus 0.5% against minus 0.3% in June. The Beige Book is the last qualitative read the committee publishes before the September meeting, and after Friday it is the first chance to see whether the districts describe the inflation the Chair described. Broadcom reports after the close - moved from Friday to Wednesday this run on the issuer's own confirmation

macro.event: ISM Services PMI; jobless claims, trade balance and revised productivity 8:30 AM
macro.note: NY Fed-confirmed. July ISM services was 54.1%. Revised productivity and unit labour costs land the same morning and matter more than usual now that the Chair has put the inflation burden on the central bank rather than on the labour market. Thursday's Fed speaker slate is still given as Waller on one calendar and Cleveland's Hammack plus Chicago's Goolsbee on another; both are reported, neither is reconciled. One honest limit carried forward: the prior claims figure of 203,000 comes from Reuters and Dow Jones rather than from the Labor Department's own page, which timed out

Triple-verified this run on the BLS empsit page, the BLS September release schedule and the NY Fed September calendar. Consensus is plus 50,000 with unemployment at 4.1%, and the attribution matters: that is the Dow Jones Newswires survey of eleven economists published Aug 28, which supersedes the Reuters plus-58,000 figure we carried yesterday. Sell-side dispersion is wide, plus 15,000 to plus 90,000, so treat any single number with suspicion. July was MINUS 23,000 payrolls with a 4.1% unemployment rate. This is the single most consequential number between now and the FOMC, it lands eleven days before that decision, and it lands into pre-holiday liquidity on the Friday before the Sept 7 Labor Day close

earnings.name: Broadcom
earnings.note: 5:00 PM ET WEDNESDAY, and this is a correction to what we published yesterday. We carried Broadcom as Friday Sept 4 on a week-ahead wire and explicitly labelled the day provisional; the issuer confirms Wednesday Sept 2, and it is Q3 fiscal 2026 rather than Q4. It is the AI-silicon read-through that matters most after Marvell's 10.28% Friday drop and Nvidia's 4.58% give-back, and it now lands two days earlier than we told you. Also due that week: Palo Alto Networks, Zscaler, Lululemon, HPE, GitLab, NetApp and Samsara
